transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-08-26 11:00am PT
- Duration: 44m
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood CSM); Lena Morales (Cortexia Lead Eng), Arjun Rao (Cortexia ML Eng), Priya Singh (Product), Michael O'Neal (Security)

Auto-summary (generated): agreed next steps around stress tests and schema for structured output. Some intermittent tool-call failures reproduced; need stronger fallbacks.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we've got 45 minutes on the calendar, a quick check-in on where the POC stands and then Jordan will drive the function-calling and output hardening items.
[00:12] Lena Morales: thanks, Maya. quick status: devs integrated the SDK last week, we're seeing 1% of calls returning malformed JSON which is blocking downstream parsers.
[00:20] Jordan Patel: ok that's what we expected, so first question: are those malformed outputs coming from the model or the client-side parsing? have you captured raw token stream?
[00:30] Arjun Rao: we have raw logs, but sometimes the SDK chopped the last bracket off, so there's a mix. also timeouts — the client retries and then we get duplicated tool invokes, which is... messy.
[00:45] Priya Singh: to add, product's acceptance criteria is strict: structured output must match schema 100% for production. we can allow a small error in dev but the POC needs to show we can get to that.
[01:02] Jordan Patel: got it. couple things: the SDK has configurable retry semantics and a verify-output hook we can enable; that hook runs a JSON schema validator before returning to the app and will attempt a 1-token re-ask if the model truncated. it's opt-in currently.
[01:18] Lena Morales: opt-in is fine, we just need it to be deterministic. are re-asks charged? how do they affect latency?
[01:26] Maya Chen: re-asks do count as extra tokens. Jordan, can you call out typical p99 impact?
[01:33] Jordan Patel: yes — small re-ask for truncated JSON usually adds ~50–120ms p50 and about 200–350ms at p99 depending on model variant. if you enable prefix/KV caching the delta drops. note: across our infra the kv cache — sometimes transcribed as K slash V cash in the logs — helps a lot for repeated contexts.
[01:53] Arjun Rao: our concern is retries causing duplicated side-effects from tool calls (e.g., duplicate DB writes). how do we prevent that?
[02:00] Jordan Patel: best practice is idempotent tool wrappers, and the SDK supports a call-id header so the backend can dedupe. additionally, we recommend function-calling confirmations: a call returns a transaction id and the SDK will verify ack before marking as complete.
[02:18] Michael O'Neal: from security side, duped writes are less of a concern than leaked PHI in logs. can you confirm logs are redacted and that KMS is used for key management?
[02:28] Maya Chen: yes, private deployments use customer-managed KMS; hosted has envelope encryption and can integrate with your KMS on dedicated. Jordan — remind them about audit log retention policy options.
[02:38] Jordan Patel: audit logs can be kept for 90/365/730 days as an add-on — and logs can be redacted at source for PII. we'll share the specific SOC2 controls doc after the call.
[02:50] Priya Singh: perfect. back to the malformed JSON — any quick mitigation for the POC while we tune model sampling?
[02:58] Jordan Patel: enable schema-guard in the SDK, set max-tokens lower and disallow sampling (use greedy/beam) for structured outputs. that usually stabilizes results. also turn on streaming + early-validate: stream tokens to your parser and if the schema looks salvageable we finish, otherwise we do a targeted re-ask.
[03:20] Lena Morales: streaming caused some surprises in our parser — intermittent chunk boundaries broke our state machine.
[03:27] Jordan Patel: yeah streaming requires robust incremental parsing; we can share a sample parser lib or you can use the SDK's built-in stream-to-JSON helper which buffers until a valid parse is found. it's a small helper in the client.
[03:40] Arjun Rao: can we get that helper?
[03:42] Jordan Patel: yes, I'll send the snippet after this sync.
[03:46] Maya Chen: cool. next, we spent some time on function/tool calling reliability in the last run — any regression numbers?
[03:56] Jordan Patel: we repro'd a failure mode where concurrent calls (50+ per second) to the same tool endpoint caused increased tail latency and occasional 502s from the tool adapter. in our environment that was due to single-threaded adapter pooling; we recommend horizontalizing the tool adapter or using Redwood's built-in batched adapter which queues and dedupes identical calls.
[04:20] Lena Morales: the tool we're calling is an internal microservice with strict RPS limits. horizontally scaling that isn't trivial. can Redwood's runtime queue requests and rate limit on our behalf?
[04:30] Jordan Patel: yes, we can route those calls through a dedicated adapter in Redwood Dedicated which respects your RPS constraints and will return a queued response. there is a tradeoff: queued responses increase latency. if latency is SLO-critical we can instead route to a dedicated pool with more tpu/gpu — sorry, I mean GPU — capacity or run the tool locally behind the VPC connector.
[04:53] Priya Singh: latency SLO for that endpoint is 150ms p99. if queueing breaches that we need to explore dedicated. what would the next step to test dedicated be?
[05:02] Diego Alvarez: we can stand up a short dedicated benchmark run — typically a 24–72 hour reservation for test. Jordan will run a p99 profile and provide numbers.
[05:12] Arjun Rao: sounds good. also noticed that when we do retries the SDK sometimes replays the tool call with slightly different payload (headers lost) which our tool rejects. is that expected?
[05:22] Jordan Patel: no, not expected. that sounds like a client-side serialization bug; please capture an example and we'll debug. SDK retries should preserve payload and headers including the call-id header.
[05:33] Lena Morales: we'll pull the trace.
[05:36] Maya Chen: quick note on model variants — you tested three: baseline-8b, baseline-8b-quant, and longcontext-compat?
[05:44] Arjun Rao: yes. baseline-8b had the fewest truncations but higher cost; quant variant had slightly worse structured output adherence, consistent with quant noise. longcontext helped with few-shot prompts but slowed p50.
[05:58] Jordan Patel: that's inline with our perf profiles. for structured output we usually recommend non-quantized for the POC and then revisit 8-bit quant for steady state if latency/cost requires it.
[06:08] Priya Singh: agreed. also, any routing policy we should enable to keep cost down in dev?
[06:14] Maya Chen: enable smart routing: dev->hosted lowest-cost model variant; canary rollouts to your dedicated pool for specific routes. Jordan will help set route policies in the console.
[06:25] Michael O'Neal: compliance question: do private deployments support SAML SSO for the internal console?
[06:31] Jordan Patel: yes, SAML SSO and enterprise RBAC are supported for Private and Dedicated. hosted supports SSO with audit logs but for strict enterprise controls we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[06:44] Arjun Rao: one more oddity: prefix caching seems to sometimes return stale KV cache items during rapid model updates. is there a TTL we can set?
[06:53] Jordan Patel: yep, caching has TTLs per-key; default is 24h in hosted but in Dedicated/Private you can tune down to seconds if you need strong freshness. also we have a cache-invalidate API for immediate evictions.
[07:06] Lena Morales: that's helpful. let's talk acceptance testing: Priya, do you have the final list?
[07:13] Priya Singh: yes—three golden tests: 1) structured output matches schema for canonical prompt set 97+% of samples; 2) no duplicate side-effect tool calls in 1000-run stress test; 3) p99 latency for critical endpoint under 200ms on the chosen deployment. once all pass we move to pilot.
[07:32] Maya Chen: thanks. Jordan — proposed stress test plan?
[07:36] Jordan Patel: plan is twofold: deterministic function-calling stress (500 concurrent, verifying no dupes with call-id), and structured-output run (10k prompts across models) to measure schema pass rates. I propose we run these in sandbox with traffic generator and share raw logs.
[07:51] Arjun Rao: can we include an end-to-end test that hits our downstream DB but with a test toggle to avoid real writes? we want to be sure the full path works.
[07:58] Jordan Patel: yes — use the SDK's dry-run mode which returns simulated tool acks without executing side-effects; that should validate the parse/handler path.
[08:07] Priya Singh: what's the plan for flaky streaming parsers? we need a robust parser lib—will Redwood share examples that handle chunk boundaries?
[08:16] Jordan Patel: yes, sample parser and the stream-to-JSON helper. we'll also provide a short sample in Typescript and Python showing incremental parse and reassembly.
[08:27] Lena Morales: great. Michael, any security blockers?
[08:30] Michael O'Neal: KMS integration needs confirmation that key material never leaves our control — if Dedicated can mount our HSM or KMS that's required. also need to confirm audit logs include tokenized request bodies masked.
[08:43] Maya Chen: agreed, we'll get the security pack. Diego will follow up with the SOC2 attachments and the KMS/HSM integration whitepaper.
[08:52] Diego Alvarez: noted, I'll attach them to the CRM thread after the call.
[08:56] Jordan Patel: quick note about telemetry — please enable request-level tracing in the SDK so we can correlate function-call id with logs; it drastically speeds debugging.
[09:06] Arjun Rao: we'll add tracing.
[09:08] Priya Singh: timing — can we expect Redwood tests by next Wednesday?
[09:12] Jordan Patel: yes I'm planning to run the stress test starting Monday and have preliminary numbers mid-week.
[09:18] Maya Chen: ok let's recap action items and owners.
[09:22] [RECAPPED ACTIONS — some overlap with action_items above]
[09:30] Lena Morales: small nit — the SDK doc reference had a typo, function-calling example used "call_id" vs our header "x-call-id"; will that cause mismatches?
[09:39] Jordan Patel: oh thanks, we'll patch the example. SDK honors both but standardizing header is important.
[09:46] Priya Singh: anything else?
[09:48] Maya Chen: no, major things covered. Next sync in one week same time unless we need an emergency follow-up after stress tests.
[09:56] Arjun Rao: thanks all.
[09:58] Meeting end.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional speaker attribution noise, timestamps approximate. Some domain terms transcribed imperfectly (e.g., "K/V cash" for KV cache). Links referenced: Redwood SDK sample snippet (shared post-call), SOC2 and KMS whitepaper (to be attached in CRM).
